title: The grapes
subtitle: Three grapes, three roles
objectives: Name the main areas for each

steps.title: Three grapes
steps.body: Pinot Noir is about 38% of plantings, Meunier about 31%, Chardonnay about 31%. Pinot Noir gives body, structure and red fruit; Meunier gives fruit and roundness; Chardonnay gives finesse, acidity and ageing potential. Four other grapes, like Arbane and Petit Meslier, are allowed but rare.

steps.title: Where each grows
steps.body: The Montagne de Reims, with Grand Crus like Aÿ, Bouzy and Verzenay, favours Pinot Noir. The Vallée de la Marne, with frost pockets and clay, suits late-budding Meunier. The Côte des Blancs, on pure chalk, with Cramant, Avize and Le Mesnil-sur-Oger, is Chardonnay country. The Côte des Bar, in the south, on Kimmeridgian marl, grows mainly Pinot Noir.
steps.highlight: Montagne, Vallée, Côte des Blancs, Côte des Bar

steps.prompt: Match each area to its main grape.

steps.body: Blanc de Blancs is made only from white grapes, usually Chardonnay; Blanc de Noirs only from black grapes, Pinot Noir and Meunier.

steps.prompt: Which grape brings finesse and ageing potential to Champagne?
steps.explanation: Chardonnay gives acidity, finesse and longevity.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Pinot Noir, Meunier and Chardonnay are Champagne's grapes
Blanc de Blancs and Blanc de Noirs use only one colour
